title: Binding of the Merlin clone design-repo to the N0 common SaaS design-constraint policy

classification.marketModel: subscription software (monthly plans with usage credits) delivered as a downloadable Mac client, sold to individual professionals (prosumer, self-serve)
audiences: individual professionals / knowledge workers on macOS
classification.decision: SaaS. Recurring subscription pricing tiers with monthly credits, subscription/billing terms and a professional (work-tool) audience are the SaaS markers the common policy assumes. It is self-serve prosumer SaaS with a desktop client rather than sales-led B2B: there is no dashboard, demo-booking or team-admin surface in the clone, so the policy's B2B-only constructs must not be introduced by a generator (see generationRules).

evidence.fact: three paid plans Pro / Ultra / Max at 29 / 99 / 299 with 25,000 / 85,000 / 250,000 credits
social proof 'Used by professionals at' (Notion, Salesforce, Harvard, HubSpot, McKinsey) - professional/work audience
'Download Merlin for Mac' - software delivered as a desktop client, not a consumer service or marketplace

classification.consideredAlternative: consumer-app (a downloadable Mac app for individuals). Rejected: the product is monetised as a recurring software subscription with usage tiers and positioned as a work tool, which is the SaaS policy's scope; nothing in the clone is a consumer service or marketplace.

generationRules: Pages are drawn only from the 7 templates and the section contracts of this design-repo; the common policy's B2B constructs that the source does not have (dashboards, demo booking, feature matrices, integration directories, changelog) must not be invented.
Pricing pages keep the real structure (3 monthly plans, exactly one primary CTA, no billing toggle); in mode=generation the tiers, prices and credits must be original (GENERATION_MODE_CLAIM).
mode=generation pages carry no Merlin brand, domain, CTA, copy, people, customers or proprietary assets (GENERATION_MODE_* rules, assets/asset-roles.json availability).
PageSpecs use approved token paths only (tokens/llm/token-policy.json, TOKEN_* rules).
contentHashRule: registry.manifest.json designPolicy.contentHash = 'sha256:' + sha256 over, for each enforcedBy path in this order, the UTF-8 path, a newline, the file bytes and a newline. extraction/verify_all.py recomputes it.

approval.note: The SaaS classification was made by an agent from the evidence above (agent attestation, not a human sign-off). A human architecture owner must ratify the binding.
